one_line: Coordinates a supply-chain disruption across buyer, supplier, and carrier portals.
what_it_does: Discovers partner tools, computes a recovery plan, stages approved actions, commits deterministically, and records audit receipts.
leverage_rationale: Structured, allowlisted tools across three independent origins create shared state, deterministic staging/rollback, and trust boundaries that UI-driving agents would handle less reliably.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies three distinct origins, explicit trust boundaries, staged commits, compensating rollback, and signed receipts.
Frames show a 480-unit delivery incident and cross-company resolution dialog.
Frame captions state three real agents and no shared backend.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent operational dashboard and resolution flow, but no video or transcript and no visibly proven completed commit.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show landing page, incident dashboard, cross-company resolution modal, and return to dashboard.
Devpost screenshot packages the project as a supply-chain planner.
impact_rationale: Supply-chain coordinators have a concrete, costly multi-party exception problem and the proposed workflow directly addresses copy-paste coordination and auditability.
impact_evidence: Hero scenario covers a 480-module Friday delivery with supplier shortage and carrier delay.
Description identifies email, spreadsheets, phone calls, and incompatible portals as current workflow.
creativity_rationale: A neutral coordination room with explicit trust boundaries, deterministic multi-party commit, and rollback is an ambitious and memorable WebMCP application.
creativity_evidence: Three-company recovery without a central backend.
Signed audit receipts and compensating rollback are pursued as core interaction concepts.
usability_note: Clear incident-centered workflow and explicit approval gate; density may challenge first-time operators.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; frames do not prove backend execution or final resolution.
standouts: Strong WebMCP indispensability through cross-origin coordination and rollback.
Concrete operational scenario.
advance_reason: High-leverage, high-impact concept with substantial visual workflow evidence despite missing end-to-end execution proof.

one_line: An agent-assisted procurement dashboard that analyzes routes and suppliers while gating purchase orders behind human approval.
what_it_does: Runs eight analyses in parallel, ranks sourcing routes, drafts a PO, and uses cryptographic approval before execution.
leverage_rationale: Parallel structured tools over supply-chain data and an approval-bound PO workflow materially improve reliability and speed over UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes eight WebMCP tools running in parallel and exclusive human PO control.
Screenshot shows agent reasoning, activity feed, route ranking, congestion, inventory, and landed-cost tools.
execution_rationale: The dashboard appears coherent and feature-rich, but the packet has no frame sheet or video and the approval/execution end state is not shown.
execution_evidence: Devpost preview visibly shows map, agent reasoning, activity feed, supplier cards, and cost/delivery figures.
Description claims PO draft and cryptographic approval queue.
impact_rationale: Procurement teams face real disruption, cost, and time pressure; route and supplier comparison is a credible direct solution.
impact_evidence: Description identifies five-plus fragmented systems and manual Excel calculations.
Visible dashboard compares congestion, prices, inventory, suppliers, and routes.
creativity_rationale: The enterprise agent-plus-human approval pattern is a strong synthesis, though the dashboard category and workflow are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Cryptographic/unforgeable approval system.
Single gesture triggering parallel multi-source analysis.
usability_note: Dashboard hierarchy, priority slider, route cards, and activity feed suggest good operational usability.
red_flags: No submitted video or frame sheets; PO approval and purchase execution are only claimed.
standouts: Readable parallel reasoning/activity evidence.
Strong human-control boundary for consequential procurement.
advance_reason: Strong practical value and WebMCP leverage, with execution confidence reduced by thin evidence.

one_line: Exposes free agent-readable market-data coverage and freshness while withholding paid data substance.
what_it_does: Registers page tools for research discovery, coverage checks, signals, teasers, and estimates without giving away the paid dataset.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the product’s agent-facing discovery and entitlement surface: it gives structured, trustworthy coverage metadata while preserving the paywall, a capability scraping cannot provide comparably.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly frames WebMCP as a fourth option between scraping, blocking, and giving data away.
Seven free tools across 49 pages report coverage, freshness, and canonical sources while withholding values.
Screenshot visibly shows named tools and tool/code framing.
execution_rationale: The editorial narrative, branding, and tool concept are coherent and visually packaged; no direct live execution is shown.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show a structured narrative from three bad options to declared tools.
Devpost screenshot shows tool names and agent-native market-research positioning.
impact_rationale: Researchers and market-intelligence buyers have a real problem discovering whether expensive data fits their question; coverage-without-leakage is directly useful.
impact_evidence: Description gives concrete streaming niches and 17,470 sourced datapoints behind paid research.
check_data_coverage returns silos, countries, years, confidence, freshness, and a value-withheld sample.
creativity_rationale: The paywalled B2B agent experience is a sharp, original WebMCP-native business model and interaction design.
creativity_evidence: Distinctive ‘free tools, paid data’ proposition.
Value withholding while exposing precise metadata is a memorable solution to agent scraping.
usability_note: The research-oriented tool taxonomy is clear, though the visual contact sheets are repetitive and text-dense.
red_flags: About text states an existing paid MCP server and 17,470 datapoints; WebMCP submission may extend pre-existing product.
standouts: Exceptional articulation of what WebMCP changes for a paywalled data business.
Strong privacy/entitlement-aware agent surface.
advance_reason: Most distinctive leverage and creativity in the packet; eligibility and newness need verification.

one_line: A shared home-goods cart where an agent proposes gifts and the user approves every purchase step.
what_it_does: Lets an agent recommend and prepare a gift in the same live cart, with page-visible approval, review, and confirmation before checkout.
leverage_rationale: Shared live cart and structured proposal/approval state are a real improvement over brittle UI automation, but general agents can reproduce much of shopping with friction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says user and ChatGPT share one live cart and nothing is placed without approval.
Screenshot shows agent-proposed and user-approved states, cart/checkout, and demo payment language.
execution_rationale: The shop, proposal card, approval state, checkout form, and safety messaging form a coherent scoped demo, though no video frames are submitted.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot visibly shows storefront, approval status, proposal, delivery fields, order summary, and non-charged demo checkout.
About text describes propose, approve, review, confirm loop.
impact_rationale: Gift shopping is a real consumer use case, and visible human control addresses a meaningful trust concern, though the scope is narrow.
impact_evidence: Concrete under-£40 cooking-gift scenario.
Explicit no-purchase-without-user approval design.
creativity_rationale: Human-supervised shared-cart commerce is useful and well executed but is a known agentic-commerce pattern.
creativity_evidence: Agent proposes instead of silently adding items.
Same-tab shared state and approval card.
usability_note: Clear proposal and checkout gates with familiar commerce affordances.
red_flags: No video frame sheets; live behavior is not independently observed.
standouts: Strong, legible human approval flow.
Demo explicitly avoids charging the user.
advance_reason: Solid safety-focused commerce workflow with credible visual packaging.

one_line: A shared catalogue and cart where the agent researches and prepares checkout but cannot finalize a purchase.
what_it_does: Provides bounded search, comparison, policy, cart, watch, and checkout tools, with autonomy and spending caps and a human-only WebAuthn buy action.
leverage_rationale: Machine-readable refusal codes, shared page state, bounded cart tools, and a deliberately unregistered final purchase action create a substantial safety/reliability delta over UI-driving agents.
leverage_evidence: Description states checkout always returns confirmation_required and confirm-purchase is not a registered tool.
Screenshot shows shared catalogue, shared cart, and agent flight recorder.
Autonomy dial and spending cap are claimed as enforced controls.
execution_rationale: The product surface is coherent and the central safety model is unusually explicit, but no public repo and no direct running proof are available in the packet.
execution_evidence: Frames show natural-language request, matching, curated recommendations, catalogue, cart, modal, and agent panel.
Devpost screenshot shows product cards, cart, controls, and flight recorder.
impact_rationale: Agentic commerce has a clear trust and accidental-purchase problem; the solution directly preserves shopper agency while retaining convenience.
impact_evidence: Description cites finalizeCart risk and contrasts scraping/private API approaches.
Human-only final purchase and visible shared cart address the stated risk.
creativity_rationale: The deliberate removal of purchase capability from the agent surface, combined with a machine-enforced autonomy dial and WebAuthn gate, is a thoughtful interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Checkout tool can never mutate cart; final click is not a tool.
Agent flight recorder and bounded controls are core product features.
usability_note: Catalogue, comparison, shared cart, and explicit checkout gate are easy to understand; safety settings add some complexity.
red_flags: No public repository and no transcript; tool invocation is inferred from UI/demo packaging.
Final purchase success is intentionally not agent-accessible.
standouts: Strongest safety-centered WebMCP design in the commerce entries.
Clear shared-state and refusal-code model.
advance_reason: High leverage and impact with a distinctive, well-evidenced safety architecture.

one_line: Packages an AI session into an encrypted, versioned link that another agent can reopen and continue.
what_it_does: Captures objective, decisions, reasoning, constraints, open tasks, sources, and hash-linked versions in a portable handoff URL.
leverage_rationale: The agent must package its live conversation in-tab and another agent must read structured handoff fields; manual transcript copying cannot preserve equivalent context, provenance, and version history.
leverage_evidence: Description explains one tool call creates a link from the current conversation with no copy/paste.
Frames show complete context, path visibility, open-anywhere, and next-version cards.
Frames show encrypted bearer token, reopening, preserved research, and context.
execution_rationale: The 173-second video transcript and frame sheets show a coherent save, reopen, inspect, contribute, and version-history workflow; exact cryptographic behavior remains claimed.
execution_evidence: Transcript narrates link creation, reopening by Codex, updating the same link, and version history.
Frames show handoff packaging, sources/decisions, portable context, and later contribution.
Devpost screenshot identifies the product and demo.
impact_rationale: Anyone moving work between agents or collaborators has a concrete context-loss problem, and preserving decisions and provenance is directly valuable.
impact_evidence: Description identifies transcript pasting and re-derivation as the current workaround.
Video narrative shows research transferred and extended by another agent.
creativity_rationale: A stateful, hash-linked, agent-to-agent handoff artifact is a highly memorable interaction model with ambitious collaboration depth.
creativity_evidence: One URL accumulates versions without overwriting.
Fields capture settled decisions and reasoning rather than only prose transcript.
usability_note: No-account single-link flow is simple for users, though bearer-link security and version semantics require careful explanation.
red_flags: Bearer-token security model is described but not independently tested in the packet.
standouts: End-to-end video evidence with agent continuation and version history.
Excellent WebMCP-native shared-state rationale.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage, impact, creativity, and unusually complete video evidence.

one_line: Learns browser workflows once, caches them as versioned skills, and repairs drifted steps.
what_it_does: Prioritizes native WebMCP, falls back to semantic DOM learning, validates reuse, detects drift, patches only failed steps, and versions the repaired skill.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP-first routing plus persistent structured capability state materially changes repeatability and reliability for agents operating changing sites.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies Native WebMCP → Cached Web Skill → browser learning ladder.
Frames show 11-action learning, validated 31ms cache reuse, drift detection, patching, version two, and native-tool priority.
Screenshot shows runtime inspector and live capability graph.
execution_rationale: The claimed learn-reuse-repair loop is visually documented with specific stages and versioning, though live functionality is still video evidence.
execution_evidence: Frame captions visibly progress from no cache to 11 semantic actions, version one, 31ms reuse, drift repair, and version two.
Devpost preview shows Observe & abstract, Memory hit, Patch failed step, and inspector.
impact_rationale: Repeated browser workflows are a broad agent reliability problem; targeted repair and reuse directly reduce token cost and brittleness for automation users.
impact_evidence: Description identifies repeated rediscovery, UI drift, and forgotten tools as pain points.
Concrete product-entry/taskboard demo demonstrates the target workflow.
creativity_rationale: Persistent semantic skills with dependency-only repair and native-tool rebinding are an ambitious, technically distinctive interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Immutable skill version history and targeted failed-step repair.
Native WebMCP and learned skills coexist in a live capability graph.
usability_note: Inspector and logs aid trust, but runtime concepts and repair states may be complex for ordinary users.
red_flags: API-key/service dependency is mentioned; no direct live test in packet.
standouts: Concrete quantified reuse and repair narrative.
Strong native-first architecture rather than WebMCP as a bolt-on.
advance_reason: Technically ambitious and well evidenced, with direct leverage on agent reliability.

one_line: A local podcast recorder where an agent proposes marker-based edits for human approval.
what_it_does: Records locally, uses recording markers to suggest removals, previews edits, supports undo, and preserves untouched originals.
leverage_rationale: Structured audio markers and approval-gated non-destructive edits make agent assistance more reliable than generic UI driving, but the outcome remains achievable with ordinary editing automation.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies WebMCP reads the finished take and returns specific regions to remove.
Screenshot shows waveform, markers, AI issues, Preview Change, Undo, and Approve Edit.
Frames show microphone, participant, marker, agent-cut, and local-dataset stages.
execution_rationale: The 21-second video is short but the product surface and workflow are coherent: setup, recording, markers, suggestions, preview, approval, and local handling.
execution_evidence: Devpost preview visibly shows waveform/timeline, edit regions, AI assistant findings, preview, undo, and approval.
Frames show German recording setup and agent-edit confirmation modal.
impact_rationale: Independent podcasters have a real editing-time bottleneck, and marker-assisted cleanup is a credible way to make production sustainable.
impact_evidence: About text describes long cleanup sessions and podcast abandonment.
Product focuses on retakes, false starts, filler, noise, and volume issues.
creativity_rationale: Capturing intent during recording through markers and applying approval-gated AI edits is a fresh, practical synthesis for podcasting.
creativity_evidence: Markers are set by the person hearing the mistake, then drive later agent suggestions.
Original audio remains untouched and edits are reversible.
usability_note: Familiar waveform review plus preview/undo/approve controls support safe editing.
red_flags: Video is only 21 seconds and exact agent invocation is not visible.
standouts: Excellent human-in-the-loop editing boundary.
Marker-driven workflow connects recording and AI cleanup cleanly.
advance_reason: Credible creative tool with a concrete workflow and good safety/usability evidence.

one_line: A communication practice simulator that gives structured feedback and retry loops for pressure situations.
what_it_does: Presents interview/workplace drills, accepts written or speaking-style responses, scores clarity/structure/vocabulary/confidence, and provides improved examples.
leverage_rationale: Structured practice tools can make agent interaction more reliable and stateful, but the core drill and feedback outcome remains achievable through a general agent with real but limited friction.
leverage_evidence: Description says the choose-drill → respond → feedback → retry loop is exposed through WebMCP tools.

execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows product positioning, practice navigation, and prompt example.
About text specifies feedback dimensions and retry loop.
impact_rationale: Interviewees and workplace communicators have a real desire to practice concise, confident responses; the proposed loop is a credible fit.
impact_evidence: Description names interviews, meetings, presentations, and difficult conversations.
Structured feedback and improved sample response address the stated difficulty.
creativity_rationale: A focused communication simulator is a useful education/productivity synthesis, but the interaction model is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Pressure-oriented drills and retry loop.
WebMCP exposes the practice workflow to an agent.
usability_note: Simple practice framing and clear start action; sign-in adds friction and the feedback flow is unshown.
red_flags: No video or frame sheets; core response and feedback loop is not demonstrated.
Sign-in is visible but access behavior is not established.
standouts: Clear audience and practice loop.
Appropriate structured dimensions for self-comparison.
advance_reason: Credible idea but thin evidence of the central workflow and only moderate WebMCP delta.

one_line: Lets agents compose bounded, personalized storefront and dashboard interfaces inside a live canvas.
what_it_does: Uses approved card presets, badges, and composable components to adapt storefront results, dashboards, and reports to a user’s needs.
leverage_rationale: The agent is not merely operating a UI; it composes a constrained user interface in shared page state, a capability general UI automation cannot provide comparably.
leverage_evidence: Description says a bounded portion of the UI is exposed for agent redesign and uses approved presets to reduce XSS risk.
Frames show a storefront recommendation request progressing to curated game results and a Live Canvas case study.
Description extends the concept to blank dashboards and saved reports.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a compelling visual concept and recommendation flow, but the frames emphasize storyboard/presentation and do not clearly prove agent composition or saved dashboard/report execution.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show natural-language request, comparing matches, building curated list, and personalized game recommendations.
Devpost screenshot shows Live Canvas overview video and paintbrush/title treatment.
impact_rationale: Adaptive interfaces can reduce discovery friction for shoppers and users of complex dashboards; the demonstrated game-discovery case has a clear entertainment use.
impact_evidence: Frames show a Monday gaming group request and tailored follow-up recommendations.
Description identifies storefront, CRM/ERP dashboard, and report-generation use cases.
creativity_rationale: Bring-your-own-interface via constrained agent composition is a genuinely original interaction idea, presented through multiple scalable cases.
creativity_evidence: Storefront redesign with approved components and agent-curated result layout.
Concept scales from bounded cards to blank dashboards and distributable datatable reports.
usability_note: Personalization promise is clear, but unconstrained dashboard composition could create discoverability and consistency challenges.
red_flags: Frames and screenshot are heavily presentation-oriented; core Live Canvas composition mechanics are not directly readable.
Some storyboard captions/claims are difficult to verify visually.
standouts: Distinctive BYOUI concept.
Constrained composition addresses safety rather than treating agent-generated UI as unrestricted HTML.
advance_reason: Highly creative and potentially high-leverage concept with a visible recommendation workflow, despite execution evidence gaps.
